svg.text: L2 domestic cells for a share 2028–30

text.tspan: L3 only if gated. The honest ceiling: ACC PLI has delivered 1.4 GWh of 50 GWh — 2.8%. Reliance Jamnagar is the LFP player (40 GWh, ramping H2
2026); Ola Cell is the only Indian producer at scale and is NMC-first.
One AC port per vehicle. AIS-138 Part 2 amended 2022 to mandate CCS2 for four-wheelers; OCPP 1.6J.
Beyond ~300 km one-way, destination charging is mandatory — a fleet-contract requirement, not a vehicle spec.
Range envelope: 268 km at 15% reserve (315 km at zero).
Feasible: Delhi–Agra 200 · Mumbai–Pune 150 · Mumbai–Nashik 170 · Bengaluru–Mysuru 145. Marginal: Delhi–Jaipur 280 (88.8% of usable).
0% road tax for life of vehicle; ₹1 lakh scrapping incentive. No purchase incentive for electric cars.
15% of ex-factory, capped ₹2 lakh, for transport e-4W — 25,000 units; 100% toll exemption on Mumbai–Pune
Expressway and Samruddhi Mahamarg; EV road-tax exempt.
20–25% capex, stamp-duty reimbursement, plug-and-play clusters. No consumer incentive.
PM E-DRIVE has no e-4W category at all.

svg.text: Both Delhi and Maharashtra expire five years before the 2035 target.
NPV at a 12% hurdle, escalated, financed, including the ₹99,000 charger.

text.tspan: Power-escalation break-even at five years: Delhi 14.5%/yr, Mumbai 8.8%, Bengaluru 8.7%. Electricity escalation is unambiguously bad for the EV in every city
(worst Mumbai −9.2 pp); the CNG leg is what carries it.
Only one cell in the entire 48-cell model is negative — Bengaluru, 5-yr, cash purchase, −0.4%.
